page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6455B processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a high base clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 60 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average middle 50% tier, indicating that workloads requiring massive parallel scaling across many cores may face tradeoffs compared to instances with higher core counts. The instance also exhibits average memory bandwidth performance, with uncached read speeds of 134.81 GB/sec and write speeds of 88.2 GB/sec.

Given its high clock speed, advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512, and substantial DDR5 memory capacity, the r7iz.4xlarge is well-suited for memory-intensive applications that require high single-threaded performance. These workloads include relational databases, memory-cached data stores, and low-latency application servers. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high-performance memory tier with dedicated CPU allocation, making it a viable choice for workloads where memory capacity and single-core speed are prioritized over raw multi-core density.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon 6455B processor with 16 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Operating at 3.9 GHz, this instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its high Geekbench single-core and text processing scores. It includes advanced hardware features such as Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions, which accelerate cryptography and vector operations. While multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, the instance provides a robust balance of high clock speed and memory density. With a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and no local storage, the r7iz.4xlarge is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, and single-thread-heavy applications that benefit from dedicated CPU resources and high-frequency execution.
